phase: PRECOMMITTED BEFORE READING projectionParity.surfaces[].permittedLoss, qualificationFixtures[].valid, or checker source
method: Read the seven canonical semantic fields, the five surface names/notes, and qualification fixture inputs. Independently decided which semantic information each surface may lose and each fixture's validity.

projectionParity.reason: This is the canonical machine projection; human rendering is not one of the seven semantic fields.

mustPreserve: termination class through its total numeric mapping
permittedLoss: error/reason code detail beyond the process code
projectionParity.reason: A scalar process status is intentionally lossy; it must never be treated as an attestation.

mustPreserve: finding count and an explicit bounded/full distinction
RunId and a retrievable route to every Finding identity
permittedLoss: inline display of every finding body and identity when a bounded summary states the omitted count and exact retrieval command
projectionParity.reason: Screen space may be bounded; semantic omission may not be silent.

mustPreserve: all seven semantic fields, using namespaced properties where SARIF has no native slot
projectionParity.reason: A machine interchange format can carry extension properties; format inconvenience is not a reason to erase semantics.

mustPreserve: all seven semantic fields across bounded pages with explicit continuation/truncation metadata
projectionParity.reason: Pagination is permitted; semantic loss is not.

knownLimitations: This derives semantic loss, not exact presentation layout.
Whether standard SARIF consumers display extension properties is a UX/interoperability measurement; retaining them in the artifact is still feasible.
The qualification outcomes do not establish that the named negative controls actually target production behavior.
